subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors — deployment-mode (Dedicated vs Private) clarifications
messages:
From: procurement@cloudbank.com
To: logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jordan.hayes@cloudbank.com
Date: 2027-01-10 09:14 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA questions for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before procurement can move forward we need a couple clarifications in the DPA:

1) Subprocessors — will you provide a current list and a cadence for updates? CloudBank policy requires either 30-day notice or the ability to object to new subprocessors that will process EU personal data.

2) Data residency / transfer mechanics — your sales slide said Dedicated = reserved GPU pools in Redwood-managed infra, Private = VPC. For Dedicated, can you confirm whether we (CloudBank) are considered controller or processor for customer data, and whether data leaves the US for any processing?

3) Execution path — do you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign? Procurement prefers a PO + DocuSign for the DPA.

Please attach the latest redline of your DPA and any subprocessors inventory.

Best,
Jordan Hayes
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudBank

From: logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
To: procurement@cloudbank.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-11 11:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions for Dedicated vs Private deployment

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3_with_logan_comments.pdf (redlines) and subprocessors_matrix_20270111.csv. High-level answers below to unblock procurement while legal reviews the redline: 

- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessors matrix and provide formal updates quarterly, with emergency notifications for on-call changes. In the redline I accepted your request for a notice window but proposed 30 days for non-critical additions and 5 days for emergency security patches; we flagged the opt-out language to avoid service interruption (see section 3.2).

- Dedicated vs Private: 
  * Dedicated (reserved capacity) = customer data is processed in Redwood-managed infrastructure dedicated to the account (isolated GPU pools and tenant network segmentation). We act as processor; replication/backup is configurable, but operational telemetry and control-plane metadata remain in Redwood control plane (US-only regions by default).
  * Private (VPC / on-prem) = control plane can be operated via our private control-plane offering; customer can choose VPC peering or on-prem package. In Private mode, customer-managed KMS and HSMs are supported; we added explicit key-escrow and BYOK language in section 5.1.

- Cross-border transfers & SCCs: we propose standard EU SCCs for EEA customer data; where customer requires, we can execute an EU addendum and support data routing to EU regions for Dedicated. Private deployments can be fully EU-hosted and avoid transfers.

- Execution: DocuSign is fine. I included a DocuSign link in the related links; procurement PO is acceptable to annotate the DocuSign envelope.

Next steps: 
- Legal to confirm the subprocessors notice cadence and opt-out semantics.
- CloudBank to confirm whether you require a hard STOP for objection (in which case we will add an escalation/oob remedial clause to preserve service).

I copied Marissa (Head of GTM Legal) and Vanessa (Head of Customer Ops) for their input on the redline points around opt-outs and KMS.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_with_logan_comments.pdf (redline, ~8 pages); subprocessors_matrix_20270111.csv

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-13 08:26 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: CloudBank redline — recommended positions and escalation path

Team — quick internal note after scanning Logan's redline:

Key redline hotspots to pre-clear with legal before DocuSign:
- Subprocessors notice & opt-out (sections 3.1–3.3): we should keep 30-day notice for non-critical subprocessors; if CloudBank insists on a full opt-out that permits them to block a subprocessor, we need a fallback: either (A) require CloudBank to accept a compatible subprocessor (list-of-approved-providers) or (B) allow Redwood to migrate workload to an alternate compatible subprocessor within 30 days while providing credits for downtime.
- Data transfer / SCCs: confirm which SCCs variant they want (controller-processor or processor-processor); add explicit routing obligations when they buy Dedicated EU-hosted capacity.
- KMS / BYOK (section 5): for Private mode we can accept customer-managed keys, but require explicit audit log access and recoverability for incident response. Add a short clause about key-rotation windows so support doesn't get blocked.
- Audit logs & eDiscovery: CloudBank asked for 3 years of audit retention in their SOW; recommend we offer 12 months standard, 36 months as a paid add-on.

Operational asks for Vanessa: if they choose Dedicated US-only but request EU servicing fallback, what's the SLA/credit structure we offer? Need to get cost delta for cross-border routing.

Next steps:
1) Vanessa to confirm operational impact and cost delta by EOD 1/14.
2) I will propose language that preserves a limited opt-out (notice + remediation window) and route that to CloudBank legal.
3) If CloudBank insists on an absolute opt-out, escalate to execs for exception approval.

Marissa
Head, GTM Legal, Redwood Inference

From: sara.gomez@cloudbank.com

Cc: procurement@cloudbank.com, jordan.hayes@cloudbank.com
Date: 2027-01-18 15:42 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors — deployment-mode (Dedicated vs Private) clarifications

Logan,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — we reviewed Redwood_DPA_v3_with_logan_comments.pdf and the subprocessors matrix. Overall the redline looks reasonable. A few points before we can execute: 

1) Subprocessors notice: CloudBank can agree to the 30-day notice for non-critical additions, but for any subprocessor that will process EEA personal data we need an explicit 30-day review period with the ability to require that CloudBank's data remain within the EEA (i.e., an opt-out for transfer out of the EEA).

2) Emergency changes: we accept faster notification for security/patching but would like a short rollback / remediation commitment.

3) SCCs variant: please confirm you will sign the controller-processor annex (we are a controller; Redwood will be a processor) — CloudBank legal needs that for audit.

4) Execution: Procurement will issue PO CB-PO-2711 for this engagement. We prefer DocuSign. Please send the envelope and reference the PO in the DocuSign comment field.

If you can incorporate the narrow EEA opt-out language and confirm the SCC annex, we can proceed to sign. We expect to complete execution within 48 hours after that change.

Sara Gomez
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
CloudBank
